title: Pagination
body:
Returning a large collection in chunks rather than all at once — food brought out in courses. The client requests a slice, typically with query parameters like `?page=2&limit=20` or `?offset=40&limit=20`, and the server returns just that slice, usually alongside metadata such as a total count or a link to the next page.

The request is made by the client but the limit is enforced by the server, which will generally cap `limit` no matter what you ask for. Offset-based pagination is simple but drifts when rows are inserted mid-scroll; cursor-based pagination (passing an opaque pointer to the last item seen) avoids that and is what infinite-scroll feeds normally use. See [[Query String]] for how the parameters are transmitted.
